Cut Optimizer

Free cut list optimizer for plywood, MDF, and paper. Enter sheet and part sizes to get a cutting layout that allows for kerf, edge trim, and grain.
H’s Notes Cut Optimizer All tools

Cut List Optimizer for Plywood, MDF, and Paper

1Material and units

Wood panels

Type lengths as 600, 23.75, 23 3/4, 23-3/4, or 4' 6 1/2". A unit after a number (mm, cm, m, in, ft) overrides the one chosen here.

2Stock sheets

 

Each row is a name, then width × length, quantity, and grain.

Width is the short side and length the long side. Grain, when ticked, runs along the length. Leave quantity empty for as many sheets as needed. Standard sizes are nominal, so measure your own stock; MDF and melamine are often sold slightly oversize.

3Parts to cut

 

Each row is a name, then width × length, quantity, and grain.

A part with grain ticked keeps its length along the grain of the sheet, so it is never turned. Parts without it may be turned 90 degrees when that saves material.

Cutting layout

Working out the layout.

4Blade and edges

 

Kerf values in the list are typical. Measure the slot your own blade leaves in a test cut. Edge trim is the distance from each factory edge to the clean edge you keep, and the trimming cut's kerf falls inside it.

5Cut sequence

 

Cuts for the sheet in the preview, in order. Point at a row to find the cut on the drawing. The fence is the distance from the edge of the piece being cut to the near side of the blade.

6Downloads and project

SVG, PNG, CSV, PDF
SVG at true scaleOpens at 1:1 in Inkscape, Illustrator, or laser and CNC software. Labels are live text in a generic sans-serif font, so convert them to outlines if your machine needs paths.
PNG pictureThe sheet in the preview as an image up to 2400 pixels wide, for a message or a quote. Not to scale.
CSV filesThe cut list with each part's sheet and position, and the cut sequence, for a spreadsheet.
PDF for the workshopEvery sheet with its cut sequence, one sheet per page. Choose Save as PDF in the print dialog.
Project fileSave the sheets, parts, and settings as a small file, and open it again later or on another computer.

7How it works

Terms and privacy

Enter the stock sheets you have and the parts you need, and the layout shows how to cut them from the fewest sheets. Tools like this are also called cut list optimizers, sheet cutting calculators, or panel layout planners.

  • Kerf is the width of material the blade turns into dust. Each part pays one kerf on the side where the next cut runs, and a part that ends at the trimmed edge pays none.
  • Rip means a cut along the length of the sheet, which is along the grain when the sheet has grain. A cross cut runs at right angles to it.
  • Every layout uses straight through cuts only, the kind a table saw, panel saw, track saw, or paper guillotine makes. These are called guillotine cuts.
  • The layout comes from a guillotine packing heuristic that tries a few hundred orderings and placement rules and keeps the best. It ranks layouts by parts left over, then sheets used, then the number of cuts. It is a good layout, not a proven minimum.
  • Nothing is sent anywhere. The current project is kept in this browser's local storage so it is still here next time, and Clear all removes it. Downloads are made on your own device.
